content: If you miss a dose of this medication, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular scheduled time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store the capsules in a refrigerator, away from light, and do not freeze them. If necessary, the capsules may also be stored at room temperature, but they must be discarded after 30 days if stored this way. Tablets should be stored at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store this medication in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in September 2024. It is important to note that this document is a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. When taking this medication, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist before starting ritonavir and each time you get a refill. Take this medication by mouth with a meal as directed by your doctor, usually one to two times daily. Take ritonavir at the same time(s) as your other HIV protease inhibitor. Swallow the tablet form of this medication whole. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition, response to treatment, and any other medications you may be taking. Inform your doctor and pharmacist about all the products you use, including prescription drugs, nonprescription drugs, and herbal products. For optimal effectiveness, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. Note that the tablet and capsule forms of this medication may deliver different amounts of the drug. It is crucial to continue taking this medication (and other HIV medications) exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Do not take more or less of this drug than prescribed, and do not stop taking it (or other HIV medicines) even for a short time unless directed to do so by your doctor. Common side effects of this medication may include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, heartburn, stomach pain, dizziness, fatigue, weakness, changes in taste, or tingling/numbness in the mouth area. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off infections you already had, potentially causing disease symptoms to reappear. You may also experience symptoms if your immune system becomes overactive. This reaction can occur at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or many months later. Changes in body fat distribution may occur while taking this medication, such as increased fat in the upper back and stomach areas and decreased fat in the arms and legs. The cause and long-term effects of these changes are unknown. A severe allergic reaction to this drug is rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking ritonavir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. This drug may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Do not drive, use machinery, or perform tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. If you have diabetes, this product may increase your blood sugar levels. Monitor your blood sugar regularly as directed and share the results with your doctor. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms of high blood sugar, such as increased thirst or urination. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant before using this medication. Treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV infection to your baby. This medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Ritonavir interacts with many medications. It can slow down or speed up the removal of other medications from your body, which may affect how they work. Similarly, other medications can affect the removal of ritonavir from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Examples include apalutamide and rifampin. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, laboratory and/or medical tests (such as liver function, viral load, T-cell counts, triglycerides/cholesterol, and blood sugar) should be performed regularly. Keep all medical and lab appointments.
